source_scope: Norfolk County, Virginia, Deed Book 9 (1710–1717), manuscript pp.332–335; Glasgow family conveyance to John Nicholls, acknowledged17September1714; FamilySearch DGS007645618, entire-film images507–510. Original register inspected25October2026.
source_reading: The original deed calls Daniel junior the eldest lawful son and heir apparent of Daniel senior and Mary, expressly his father and mother. They were of Moyock in North Carolina; the land lay above the Southern Branch Great Bridge in Norfolk County, Virginia. The80-acre tract is explicitly the property granted to Daniel senior and Mary by John Gamon’s will of4October1693, recorded15March1693/4, with remainder to Daniel’s bodily heirs by Mary, Gamon’s daughter. Daniel senior, Mary and Daniel junior acknowledged the deed in Norfolk court on17September1714. This completes the1693→1714 Richford Swamp title bridge and establishes the parent–child relationship. The later1733 and1752 dates are contingent redemption/lease endpoints, not execution dates.
identity_decision: The documentary son is distinct from his father. Glasgow-3322 represents the1693 Mary Gamon husband and is therefore the98% confident father identification for this record-defined son. Glasgow-1158 also carries Mary Gammon as wife and may duplicate the senior account; assigning it to junior would turn that wife into his mother without resolving the identity conflict. Keep both current profiles and their existing parents; do not merge or reparent them. The1718–1719 Currituck Senior/Junior taxpayers are probably this Moyock father and son (85% identity assessment), supported by the close locality, same unusual names and four-to-five-year continuity, but the tax lists alone do not identify their land. The1729 Slade100-acre tract remains separate; William-428’s father remains42%, Daniel-1158→Robert-1157 remains12%, and Daniel-3322→Robert-1157 remains34%. No Scottish ancestry, exact birth or maternal maiden name beyond the explicit Gamon daughter identification is inferred.
